newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to issue $750 million in bonds this week.
newsitem.headline: Israel to issue $750 million in bonds this week.

text.p: Israel will raise $750 million in the United States this week in the framework of the U.S. loan guarantee programe, the Treasury said on Sunday.
It said director-general David Brodet, accountant-general Shai Talmon and his deputy Avi Elkind are in the United States to decide the underwriter and oversee the offering.
Treasury sources have said Israel will raise with U.S. guarantees about $1.35 billion annually this year and next, the last two years of the guarantees programme.
Since 1993, the Treasury said, Israel had borrowed $6.6 billion of the $10 billion it is permitted to raise with U.S. guarantees.
From that amount, Washington U.S. deducts what it says Israel invests in West Bank settlements. For 1997 and 1998, the deduction is $60 million per year.
Israel last raised $920 million with U.S. backing in August 1996.

Last month the country made its first Eurobond offering without American guarantees, raising $200 million out of a planned $750 million over three years. At the end of 1995, it made a $250 million Yankee bond offering.
Both issues were to test the waters for future Israeli debt offerings after the guarantees run out.
